newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Township rivals cut Jianshe's 1996 net.
newsitem.headline: Township rivals cut Jianshe's 1996 net.

text.p: Cheap motorcycles churned out by township firms helped depress Shenzhen North Jianshe Motorcycle Co Ltd's 1996 profits, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.

"Cheap township-made motorcycles flooded China's market and cut Jianshe's market share to six percent last year from 13 percent in 1995," the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Jianshe posted a net profit of 50.73 million yuan for 1996 against 288.71 million yuan for 1995 based on international accounting standards.
The company was forced to slash sale prices of its core products, 50-60 cc models, and increase commissions to sales agents to preserve market share, the official said.
The price cut and higher commissions cost the firm nearly 300 million yuan in 1996, he said.
Jianshe made 570,000 motorcycles in 1996, down from 1.03 million in 1995, the official said. China's national output jumped to about 10 million motorcycles in 1996 from 7.8 million in 1995.
Earnings were also hurt in 1996 after Chinese authorities ordered a halt to moped production to help fight pollution, he said.
Jianshe's turnover dropped to 2.49 billion yuan in 1996 from 3.61 billion in 1995.
The company reduced production of 50-60 cc models and increased production of both 80 cc and 150 cc models in a bid to boost profitability, the official said.
Jianshe aims to sell 790,000 motorcycles in 1997, more than half of them 80 cc models and 20,000 of them 150 cc models, he said.
The output of 80 cc models reached 360,000 last year, while production of 150 cc models was only 200, the official said.
Jianshe has a $79 million evenly-owned venture with Yamaha Motor Co Ltd in southwestern China's Sichuan province.
Yamaha has aided Jianshe with technology for production of the 150 cc model after setting up the venture in 1993, he said.
Jianshe expects higher earnings in 1997 on better sales and wider profit margins, the official said. He declined to give a specific forecast.
Jianshe was the strongest performer in the B share market on Tuesday, when it closed at its 10 percent limit-up at HK$3.81 on volume of 827,100 shares.
"Although the firm's results were terrible, they beat expectations as the motor industry has had a rough year," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
